sh.title: Shield
sh.hero.0.sub: Neither the firewall nor the DNS blocker is on. Turn one on to protect this server and your network.
sh.hero.1.sub: One of the two protections is on. Turn on the other for full coverage.
sh.hero.2.sub: The firewall is on and ads and trackers are blocked for every device that uses this server.
sh.fw.onHint: Incoming connections are checked against your rules.
sh.fw.offHint: Every listening port can be reached by other devices.
sh.fw.onMsg: Your connection stays open: {client} keeps access on ports {ports}. You will have one minute to keep the change, or it is undone automatically.
sh.fw.offMsg: Every listening port becomes reachable from the network again.
sh.fw.safe: Lock-out protection: {client} always keeps access to ports {ports}.
sh.fw.unsupported: The firewall needs NoCapOS running on Linux as root.
sh.fw.notInstalled: ufw, the firewall engine Shield controls, is not installed.
sh.fw.installYourself: NoCapOS cannot install packages on this system. Install ufw manually, then reopen Shield.
sh.keep.title: Keep these changes?
sh.keep.body: If you can still see this, choose Keep. The change is undone in {n} s.
sh.ov.liveHint: One bar per minute. Red shows blocked queries.
sh.ov.allowWarn: Incoming connections are allowed by default. Consider setting the default to deny and allowing only what you need.
sh.exp.title: What's exposed
sh.exp.hint: Services listening for other devices, and whether the firewall lets them through.
sh.exp.hintOff: The firewall is off, so all of these are reachable. Switches apply once it is on.
sh.exp.none: No services are listening for other devices.
sh.exp.bypass: published by the container engine, which bypasses ufw
sh.exp.closeMsg: Other devices will no longer reach {port}.
sh.preset.title: Presets
sh.preset.hint: Allow common services with one click.
sh.rule.title: Rules
sh.rule.hint: Rules are checked in order; the first match applies.
sh.rule.none: No rules yet. The default policies apply.
sh.rule.limitHint: Limit allows the connection but blocks addresses that try 6 or more times within 30 seconds. Useful for SSH.
sh.dns.offHint: Off by default. Turn it on and point your devices at this server to block ads and trackers.
sh.dns.onMsg: NoCapOS will answer DNS on port 53 and download the enabled block lists. Devices are not affected until you point them at this server.
sh.dns.useHereHint: This server's own DNS lookups also go through the blocker.
sh.dns.useTitle: Use the blocker on this server?
sh.dns.useMsg: This server will resolve names through the blocker. If the blocker stops, NoCapOS switches it back.
sh.p53.title: Port 53
sh.p53.hint: The system resolver holds port 53 on loopback. Free it so the blocker can listen on every address.
sh.p53.freedHint: NoCapOS has freed port 53 from the system resolver. You can restore it at any time.
sh.p53.lanNote: The blocker currently listens on this machine's own addresses only, which is enough for devices on your network.
sh.p53.freeMsg: The system resolver stops listening on port 53. This machine keeps resolving names as before.
sh.setup.title: Point your devices at the blocker
sh.setup.hint: Only devices that use this server for DNS are protected.
sh.setup.router: Recommended: in your router's settings, set the DNS server (usually under DHCP or LAN).
sh.setup.devices: Alternatively, set it per device in its Wi-Fi or network settings.
sh.setup.check: Reconnect the device, then check the Logs tab to confirm its queries arrive.
sh.lists.title: Block lists
sh.lists.hint: {n} domains are blocked, including their subdomains.
sh.lists.removeMsg: Its domains will no longer be blocked.
sh.allow.title: Allow list
sh.allow.hint: Domains here are never blocked, even if a list contains them.
sh.block.title: Custom block list
sh.block.hint: Your own blocked domains, one per line. Subdomains are included.
sh.rec.title: Local DNS records
sh.rec.hint: Answer names on your network yourself, such as nas.home.
sh.logs.privacy: Stored only on this server. You can turn it off or shorten retention in Settings.
sh.logs.off: The query log is turned off.
sh.logs.clearMsg: All stored queries will be permanently deleted.
sh.logs.devicesHint: Devices seen in the last 24 hours. Select one to view its queries.
sh.logs.blockedHint: Connections the firewall refused in the last 24 hours (requires firewall logging).
sh.logs.noBlocked: No blocked connections, or firewall logging is off.
sh.set.upstreamsHint: Where allowed queries are sent, tried in order. One per line.
sh.set.kinds: Plain DNS: 9.9.9.9 · DNS-over-TLS: tls://1.1.1.1 · DNS-over-HTTPS: https://1.1.1.1/dns-query
sh.set.cnamesHint: Also block answers that point to a blocked domain.
sh.set.privacyHint: The query log never leaves this server.
sh.set.logHint: Required for top domains and the per-device view.
sh.set.logClientsHint: When off, the log stores domains without device addresses.
sh.set.ipv6Hint: Apply the rules to IPv6 traffic as well. Recommended.
